message.content:
Add REAL PDF invoices to the Nxeon platform. Work EXCLUSIVELY in /opt/nxeon-wt-invoicepdf (branch feature/gap-invoicepdf). node_modules symlinked. Do NOT run build/prisma commands — code only. Do NOT touch order/renewal charge logic (another agent is on the money core) — this is invoice RENDERING/delivery only.

CONTEXT: Today invoices are print-ready HTML — lib/mailer.ts:90 says "There is no PDF library installed (and we can't add dependencies)". That constraint is lifted: you MAY add a dependency. lib/invoices.ts builds the invoice HTML (invoiceCreateData + a print view ~:379). Customers currently must Print→Save-as-PDF; accounting depts need a real attached PDF.

BUILD:
1. Add a server-side PDF renderer. Prefer a lightweight, dependency-light path: use an HTML→PDF approach that works headless on the server. Options in order of preference: (a) if the app already has a headless browser available reuse it; (b) otherwise add a self-contained library — `@react-pdf/renderer` (React→PDF, no system deps) is a good fit for a Next.js server action/route, or `pdfkit`. Avoid puppeteer/playwright if it needs a full Chromium download unless nothing else fits. Add it to package.json.
2. Generate the PDF from the existing invoice data (reuse the invoice model + the same branded layout/line-items the HTML uses — logo, from/to, line items, totals, tax breakdown line if present, paid status, period). Keep it visually consistent with the existing branded HTML invoice.
3. A **download endpoint/action**: an authenticated route (e.g. app/api/invoices/[id]/pdf) that streams the PDF, ownership-checked (caller owns the invoice or is admin) — mirror the guards on the existing invoice view/route. Add a "Download PDF" button on the invoice UI (app/dashboard/invoices + the invoice detail/billing page).
4. **Attach the PDF** to the invoice/receipt/renewal emails: update lib/mailer.ts (~:85-110) so where it currently attaches the print-ready HTML it now ALSO (or instead) attaches the real PDF. Keep the email body as-is; just add the PDF attachment.

Keep it clean and self-contained; don't change what an invoice CONTAINS or any charge amount — only how it's rendered/delivered. DELIVER, then commit `git add -A && git commit -m "feat: real PDF invoices (server-rendered, download + email attachment)"` (trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>), `git push -u origin feature/gap-invoicepdf`. REPORT (factual): the PDF library chosen + why, files changed, the download route + its ownership guard, and where the PDF is attached to emails. Don't claim tested.

content.text:
Committed and pushed. Here is the factual summary.

## Real PDF invoices — delivered

**PDF library chosen: `pdfkit` (^0.15.1) + `@types/pdfkit` (dev)**
Why: pure-JS generator with no headless browser and no system libraries; it embeds the standard Helvetica fonts (no font files to ship), so it runs headless in a Next.js Node route. It draws imperatively, which let me reproduce the existing branded HTML invoice faithfully. Playwright was present but only as a devDependency and would require a Chromium binary; `@react-pdf/renderer` risked React-19 peer friction. Nothing PDF-related was already installed, so `pdfkit` was added to package.json (not installed — I did not run install/build per instructions).

**Files changed**
- `lib/invoice-pdf.ts` (new) — `renderInvoicePDF(invoice, user, branding): Promise<Buffer>` and `invoicePdfFilename()`. Reuses `invoiceTotals` / `formatInvoiceNumber` / `brandLabel`, so it renders only and never derives a charge amount. Mirrors the HTML layout: gradient top bar, "N" logo mark, From/Billed-to/Issued/Service-period blocks, itemised table, subtotal/tax/total, refunded line, and the colored status stamp (PAID/OPEN/VOID/REFUNDED).
- `app/api/invoices/[id]/pdf/route.ts` (new) — the download endpoint.
- `components/customer/InvoiceViews.tsx` — new `DownloadInvoicePdfButton` (anchor to `/api/invoices/[id]/pdf`).
- `app/dashboard/invoices/[id]/page.tsx` — "Download PDF" button in the header.
- `app/dashboard/invoices/page.tsx` — per-row "PDF" action (kept existing HTML "Download" alongside).
- `lib/mailer.ts` — `invoiceAttachment()` now builds a real PDF instead of print-ready HTML.
- `package.json` — added `pdfkit` + `@types/pdfkit`.

**Download route + ownership guard**
`GET /api/invoices/[id]/pdf` (pinned `runtime = "nodejs"`). Guards mirror the existing HTML route exactly: `currentUser()` required (401 if none), 404 if the invoice is missing, and `isOwner = invoice.userId === user.id || isAdmin (user.role === "ADMIN")` — otherwise 403. Streams `application/pdf` with `Content-Disposition: attachment` and `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

**Where the PDF attaches to emails**
`lib/mailer.ts` → `invoiceAttachment(invoiceId)`, called from `sendMail` when `opts.invoiceId` is set and the template is in `INVOICE_ATTACH_TEMPLATES` (`receipt`, `invoice_new`, `renewal_reminder`). It now returns `{ filename: nxeon-invoice-INV-#####.pdf, content: <Buffer>, contentType: "application/pdf" }`, using the same `invoiceBranding()`. Email bodies were left unchanged; the print-ready HTML attachment was replaced by the real PDF.

Charge/renewal logic was not touched — this is rendering/delivery only. Not tested (no build/install run per instructions). Committed as `3677c0f` and pushed to `origin/feature/gap-invoicepdf`.

Note: two flagged environment issues unrelated to the task — the Figma MCP server needs authorization, and one Bash classifier call briefly failed before I retried successfully.
